# Esbjerg: Børne- og Ungdomspsykiatrisk Ambulatorium

Esbjerg: Børne- og Ungdomspsykiatrisk Ambulatorium is a child and adolescent psychiatric outpatient department located in [[region-syddanmark|Region Syddanmark]], one of Denmark's five health regions [^src1] [^src2] [^src3]. The clinic appears repeatedly in the national [[adhd-databasen|ADHD-databasen]] quality registry's annual reports for 2023 and 2024, which track how well child and adolescent psychiatric departments across Denmark meet clinical quality standards for ADHD diagnosis and treatment [^src9].

The department's most notable documented result is a 78% compliance rate (95% CI: 56-93) for clinical environmental observation among 0-5 year olds, reported against 18 of 23 relevant cases, in the ADHD_2023 report [^src1]. This is a comparatively strong figure by the database's usual standards, though the surrounding context describes Region Syddanmark overall as experiencing a marked decline in this period — a decline the database's steering group attributes largely to staffing shortages at the Esbjerg and Vejle clinics specifically, stating that "Faldet i Region Syddanmark skyldes et stort fald på afdelinger i Esbjerg og Vejle formentlig betinget af færre lægekræfter her" [^src1]. This links Esbjerg's performance directly to [[vejle-boerne-ungdomspsykiatrisk-ambulatorium|Vejle: Børne- og Ungdomspsykiatrisk Ambulatorium]] as a co-cause of the regional trend.

Beyond this headline figure, the clinic's results varied considerably across the different quality indicators tracked by the database. In the 2023 report, Esbjerg achieved only 11% compliance on Indikator 3, drawn from 304 udredningsforløb — "Esbjerg: Børne- og Ungdomspsykiatrisk Ambulatorium opnåede 11 % opfyldelse af Indikator 3 blandt 304 udredningsforløb" [^src2] — and 45% compliance (38-52%, 90 of 202 pathways) on Indikator 4 concerning coordinating network meetings, per the claim that "Esbjerg havde 45 % opfyldelse af indikator 4 (95% CI: 38-52) med 90 forløb ud af 202" [^src3]. A further metric in the same report shows 14% (10-20%, 29 of 202 pathways) [^src4]. The clinic also reported that 103 of 304 pathways (34%) included somatic examination [^src14].

In the follow-up ADHD_2024 report, covering the period 01.04.2024-31.03.2025, Esbjerg's results shifted again: 75% (68-81%, 155 of 207 pathways) on one measure [^src5], 12% (8-17%, 27 of 222 pathways) on another [^src6], and notably 52% (45-59%, 117 of 224 pathways) on a further indicator — a figure singled out in the report as the highest among departments with at least three pathways nationwide, where "Ingen afdelinger nåede udviklingsmålet og resultaterne blandt afdelinger med minimum tre forløb varierede fra 1 % på BUA Psykiatrisk Klinik for Unge til 52 % på PSY Børne- Og Ungdomspsykiatrisk Ambulatorium (Esbjerg)" [^src7], contrasting Esbjerg with [[bua-psykiatrisk-klinik-unge|BUA Psykiatrisk Klinik for Unge]]. Additional 2024 figures include 10% (6-14%, 22 of 224) [^src8], 62% (55-68%, 139 of 224) [^src9], 25% (3-65%, denominator unspecified) [^src10], and 50% (16-84%, 4 of 8) [^src11], along with a bare mention without accompanying figures on page 63 of the 2024 report [^src12].

Taken together, these figures place Esbjerg among the many Danish child and adolescent psychiatric departments whose performance on the ADHD-databasen's quality indicators — most of which carry a 90% national development target — falls well short of that standard on most measures, even where the clinic occasionally posts comparatively strong results such as the 78% and 75% figures noted above [^src1] [^src5]. The broader ADHD-databasen reports describe this pattern nationally as driven by staffing pressures, rising referral volumes, and changing registration practices across regions [^src9].
